title: Seconds and thirds
summary: Intervals name the distance between two notes. Start with the small ones.

steps.title: What an interval is
steps.body: An **interval** is the distance between two notes. Musicians name it with a number and a word, like "major 3rd". The name tells everyone exactly how far apart two notes are, and you can always work it out by counting half steps.

steps.title: Seconds
steps.body: You already know two intervals. A half step is also called a **minor 2nd**, and a whole step is a **major 2nd**. Minor is the smaller one, major the bigger one.

steps.title: Thirds
steps.body:
Three half steps make a **minor 3rd** (C to E♭). Four half steps make a **major 3rd** (C to E).

Thirds are what chords are built from. A major 3rd sounds bright and a minor 3rd sounds darker. That is most of the difference between a major chord and a minor chord.

steps.title: Thirds above C
steps.body: E♭ is a minor 3rd above C, and E is a major 3rd above C.

items.prompt: Play C4, then go up a major 3rd.
Play C4, then go up a minor 3rd.
Play G4, then go up a major 3rd.
Play D4, then go up a minor 3rd.
Play E4, then go up a major 2nd.

steps.title: Slide a pair of thirds
steps.body: Hold two white keys a 3rd apart, like C and E, and slide the pair up one white key at a time. Some pairs are major 3rds and some are minor. Listen for bright and dark.

items.prompt: Play F4, then go up a major 3rd.
Play E4, then go up a minor 2nd.
